Source: https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Palpatine/Legends
Scope: Combat, Force-power, survival, and scaling statements copied from the article. Article citation markers in square brackets are retained. Politics/navigation omitted. “Statement—not feat” labels distinguish rankings, character opinions, and comparisons from observed actions.

THE TRAINING OF DARTH MAUL

- “In 37 BBY, the time came for Maul's final test. Sidious sent him out to Hypori, where he was hunted by assassin droids for a month. At the end of the month, Maul found Sidious waiting at the mouth of a cave. He had not eaten for days, and was exhausted. Regardless, Sidious challenged Maul to a duel, in which he easily evaded each of Maul's attacks.” [41][43]
  Source: Star Wars Journal: Darth Maul ; The Wrath of Darth Maul [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 41,43; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Enraged, Maul gathered all the dark side could offer within him and flew at Sidious with murderous intent. Sidious was caught off guard, but had managed to struggle through the onslaught before disarming Maul. Even without a weapon, Maul continued to attack, even going so far as to bite Sidious' hand before being ultimately defeated.” [41][43]
  Source: Star Wars Journal: Darth Maul ; The Wrath of Darth Maul [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 41,43; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]

THE RISE OF SENATOR PALPATINE (52–32 BBY)

- “Palpatine proceeded to slaughter every being present, saving Teem to last: using the Force, he ignited the room's curtains and collapsed them on to the Gran, burning Pax Teem to death.” [1]
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 1; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]

THE FALL OF CHANCELLOR VALORUM

- “With his master's guard completely down, Palpatine betrayed Plagueis by blasting his transpirator mask with Force lightning, shorting it out and waking him; being inebriated and half-asleep, however, the Muun could do nothing to stop his apprentice.” [1]
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 1; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “And throughout the relentless derision, Sidious sent forth additional blasts of lightning, causing the Muun immense pain as he slowly suffocated.” [1]
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 1; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]

CLONE WARS (22–19 BBY): MAUL, SAVAGE OPRESS, AND TALZIN

- “Sidious Force-choked two members of the Shadow Collective” and “two of his guards were lifted into the air and Force-choked to death.” [101][104]
  Source: The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy ; Star Wars: The Clone Wars — "The Lawless" [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 104,101; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Sidious proved himself to be a match for their combined strength” when fighting Maul and Savage Opress with two lightsabers. “After using the Force to temporarily incapacitate Maul, Sidious then toyed with Opress, dodging all of his blows without having his lightsabers ignited, before he started to duel Opress. Completely outclassing him, he impaled the larger Zabrak in the chest with his two lightsabers within just a minute, fatally wounding him.” [101][104]
  Source: The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy ; Star Wars: The Clone Wars — "The Lawless" [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 104,101; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Maul found himself being pressured in a bladelock. But via all his Force augmentation, he turned the tides against his former apprentice and forced his blades down Maul's sabers before forcing them apart and away, disarming Maul.” Sidious then “launched a barrage of his Force lightning at Maul.” [101][104]
  Source: The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy ; Star Wars: The Clone Wars — "The Lawless" [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 104,101; approximate match 0.86, verify; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Talzin at first decided to posses Dooku's body and engaged Sidious, with her lack of training in lightsaber combat, the fight was a quick one and the Sith easily disarmed her and shot force lightning at her forcing her to come out of Dooku's body.” Sidious then fought Talzin in a Force struggle; Dooku added his lightning, and Grievous executed Talzin. [108]
  Source: Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 4 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 108; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]

ENDGAME (19 BBY): MACE WINDU

- “Declaring treason, Sidious pulled out an electrum saber of his own design hidden in his sleeve.” He “killed Masters Kolar and Tiin before they could defend themselves,” then slew Kit Fisto “only moments later.” [13]
  Source: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 13; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Left alone with Windu, the Dark Lord fought him in a ferocious one-on-one lightsaber duel.” The article says Windu’s Vaapad countered Sidious’s Form VII; “After several minutes of intense dueling, Windu overpowered and disarmed Sidious, then held him at blade point.” [13]
  Source: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 13; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “When Windu declared that the threat of the Sith would never return and that Sidious had lost, the Sith Lord angrily fired torrents of Force lightning at the Jedi Master.” Windu deflected it back, disfiguring and injuring Sidious. After Anakin severed Windu’s sword arm, “Sidious…assaulted Windu with a devastating blast of Force lightning and hurled the Jedi Master from the building to his death far below.” [13][110][111][112]
  Source: Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith - Interview with Ian McDiarmid on outnow.ch (backup link) ; About.com: Hollywood Movies » Ian McDiarmid on Playing the Most Evil "Star Wars" Character of the Franchise on movies.about.com (backup link) ; "The Evil Within" — Star Wars Insider 82 ; Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 110,111,112,13; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]

THE FALL OF THE CIS / LAST STAND OF THE JEDI ORDER: YODA

- “There, the Dark Lord of the Sith and the Grand Master of the Jedi Order dueled in a battle that destroyed a good portion of the Grand Convocation Chamber.” Sidious stated that Vader “will become more powerful than either [Yoda or Sidious]”; Yoda said Sidious’s faith would be misplaced. This is a character prediction/opinion, not an observed feat. [13]
  Source: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 13; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “The two combatants demonstrated amazing strength and skill in the Force, as well as incredible lightsaber prowess. They were at first evenly matched,” but “Yoda had slowly began to outclass Sidious.” Sidious was “incapable of matching the Jedi Master's nigh-unrivalled swordsmanship for long.” [13][116]
  Source: Star Wars: Jedi Battles ; Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 116,13; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Eventually, the battle progressed to greater levels when the Emperor was deprived of his lightsaber and forced to use the Force to keep Yoda away.” Sidious blasted Yoda’s lightsaber away with lightning; Yoda used Tutaminis to deflect it. [13][114]
  Source: Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith junior novelization [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 114; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Sidious advanced on Yoda, steadily strengthening the power of his lightning,” but Yoda redirected it; the combined powers caused an explosion that hurled both apart. [13]
  Source: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 13; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Overmatched and defeated, Yoda fled.” [13][73]

THE EMPEROR’S REIGN (19 BBY–4 ABY)

- “At some point after the declaration of the Empire, Emperor Palpatine ordered five captured Jedi to be brought before him.” He handed each a lightsaber; when four attacked him, “he cut three of them down simultaneously.” The surviving Jedi were the Human female and the Verpine Beyghor Sahdett. [119]
  Source: Dark Times—A Spark Remains 3 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 119; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Byss was a dark side conduit, able to invigorate practitioners of the dark side by flooding them with Force energy. Along with the power of Byss, Palpatine slowly fed on the life energy of his workers in order to lengthen his own life.” [131][132]
  Source: Evasive Action: Recruitment ; The Essential Atlas [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 131,132; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]

THE BALANCE OF THE FORCE / PALPATINE’S BATTLE MEDITATION

- Palpatine’s Force lightning attack on Luke: “Raising his arms, Palpatine released a withering barrage of Force lightning that tore through the boy and brought him to his knees.” Luke could not repel or block it, and the Emperor increased its intensity. [179]
  Source: Star Wars: Return of the Jedi novelization [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 179; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Without warning, Anakin grabbed Palpatine from behind,” and Palpatine’s own bolts electrocuted him and damaged Anakin’s life-support systems. Anakin then threw Palpatine down the shaft; “Shortly after hitting the reactor, still discharging his force lightning, Palpatine then exploded into dark side energy.” [5][47][181]
  Source: Star Wars: Complete Locations ; Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 47,5; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “It was within Palpatine's power to use the dark side to control his forces, even across great distances.” The article says that at Endor Palpatine was occupied trying to turn Luke, and Grand Admiral Declann—not Palpatine—used dark-side battle meditation to improve the fleet’s coordination. [179]
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

PALPATINE REBORN (4–11 ABY)

- “At an unknown time prior to his death at the Battle of Endor, Palpatine had found a different way to cheat death by preserving his spirit after the death of his body, by the method of essence transfer.” He prepared clones on Byss for his spirit to possess; the bodies deteriorated progressively faster. [19][134]
  Source: Dark Empire 2 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 19; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “After the destruction of the second Death Star, Palpatine's spirit was forced to journey in the maddening, bodiless existence of the void,” eventually possessing Jeng Droga and then a clone of himself. [19][77]
  Source: Dark Empire 2 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 19; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Using his dark powers to create a powerful Force storm, he swept Luke Skywalker to Byss.” [19][192]
  Source: Dark Empire 2 ; Dark Empire 1 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 19,192; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Palpatine quickly attempted to turn” Leia and revealed that he planned to transfer his mind into her unborn child. [7]
  Source: Dark Empire 5 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 7; approximate match 0.90, verify; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Before he could finish the job, Palpatine transferred his spirit into one of the last clones.” “However, even Luke's skills with Djem So were not enough, and he fell before Palpatine's brutally intense swordplay.” [7]
  Source: Dark Empire 5 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 7; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- In the later encounter, “Despite Palpatine's viciousness, Luke managed to defeat the Dark Lord in a brief but intense lightsaber duel, slicing off his hand.” [8]
  Source: Dark Empire 6 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 8; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Palpatine was hardly finished, summoning a Force storm against the New Republic fleet.” Leia and Luke, aided by the unborn Anakin Solo, severed his connection to the Force; the uncontrolled storm destroyed Eclipse and killed Palpatine again. [8]
  Source: Dark Empire 6 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 8; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “He used essence transfer not only as a pathway to immortality, but also as a particularly cruel and sadistic form of torture; it is known that he killed and resurrected Imperial engineer Bevel Lemelisk seven times as punishment for the destruction of the first Death Star.” [164]
  Source: Dark Empire 2 ; Darksaber [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 19,164; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “The entire population of Byss lived under this spell until the planet's destruction by the Galaxy Gun.” The preceding power description says Palpatine could channel the collective life essences of billions to sustain himself and his Dark Side Adepts. [21][265][266]
  Source: The Essential Atlas [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 265; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- At the final confrontation, “Palpatine killed Ysanna instantly and fatally wounded Brand,” before Han Solo shot him. Brand then bound Palpatine’s soul to his own departing life force and dragged it into the depths of the Force. [9]
  Source: Empire's End 2 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 9; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]

POWERS AND ABILITIES: ARTICLE-WIDE SCALING STATEMENTS (STATEMENTS, NOT FEATS)

- “Darth Sidious was considered by many, including Darth Vader and Luke Skywalker, to be the most powerful Sith Lord in the entire history of the Sith—something he himself firmly believed.” [1][39][134][223]
  Source: Dark Empire endnotes ; Vader: The Ultimate Guide ; Darth Plagueis ; Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith novelization [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 134,223,1,39; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “He was also considered the one Force user to have successfully tamed the Dark Side of the Force, exceeding even that of Ulic Qel-Droma.” [133]
  Source: Dark Empire Sourcebook [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 133; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “It seems that only Yoda had the Force abilities required to single-handedly duel Sidious to a standstill, although even that was not enough to defeat the Dark Lord.” [13]
  Source: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 13; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Another single individual who was able to briefly hold Palpatine was Galen Marek, but only through the Sith Lord wanting to turn, not kill Marek.” [26]
  Source: Star Wars: The Force Unleashed [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 26; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- The article calls Dooku “one of the most talented and powerful Force adepts in the galaxy” and says that among his Jedi peers “only Grandmaster Yoda was considered his superior as a swordsman.” [1]
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 1; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Despite his frail appearance, Darth Sidious was immensely skilled in lightsaber combat, having mastered every conceivable form by the time of the Clone Wars.” [224]
  Source: Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Episode Guide [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 224; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “As a result of his tremendous skill, and use of the Force to gain an edge, he effortlessly killed Agen Kolar and Saesee Tiin—who were considered to be two of the finest lightsaber duelists of their time—each with a single blow,” and slew Kit Fisto while engaged with Windu. [13][39]
  Source: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith ; Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith novelization [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 13,39; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Many years later, Palpatine, moments after coming back in one of his clone bodies, engaged and defeated Luke Skywalker in a hard-fought one-on-one lightsaber duel” and “barely lost” the second encounter; Luke’s victory was aided by Leia’s Force Harmony. [7][8]
  Source: Dark Empire 5 ; Dark Empire 6 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 7,8; approximate match 0.94, verify; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “In fact, the only people known to have even disarmed him in lightsaber combat were Mace Windu, Yoda, and (in the literal sense) Luke Skywalker.” [7][8][13][114]
  Source: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith ; Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith junior novelization ; Dark Empire 6 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 13,114,8; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Yoda considered him to be the most powerful darksider the Grandmaster had ever faced.” [114]
  Source: Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith junior novelization [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 114; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Palpatine was incredibly skilled in Force lightning and was known to use this both as a lethal attack, and as a way of torturing his enemies.” The article says he could instantly reduce one or more people to charred husks if used at full potency. [5][117]
  Source: Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 5; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- The article lists lightning against Plagueis, Maul, Talzin, Windu, Yoda, dozens of stormtroopers, Garrbo V’Droz, Bothans, Luke, Leia, Brand, and Ysanna. These are feats described in the Force powers section, with citations [1][5][8][9][13][21][26][101][104][108][114][117][151][164][194][226][227][228][229].
  Source: UNRESOLVED (sentence not found in current Wookieepedia article revision; primary source not identified)
- “Another very dangerous and advanced Force technique utilized by the Emperor was the ability to use the Force to transfer his essence, as well as the essences of others, which he used to survive death on at least three occasions.” [7][19][20][133][164]
  Source: Dark Empire Sourcebook ; Darksaber ; Dark Empire 2 ; Dark Empire 5 ; Dark Empire II 1 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 133,164,19,7,20; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Palpatine was also the only known being capable of producing a Force storm of his own power, a dark side technique which he himself discovered, and that had enough power to kill an entire world.” [192][240]
  Source: The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 240; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- The same passage says the storm could rip the space-time continuum into a hyperspace wormhole; early in learning it Palpatine admitted he could not fully control it, while by 10 ABY he could send several storms at will. A fully powered storm required Luke, Leia, and the unborn Anakin Solo’s combined light-side effort to turn it against him. [8][134]
  Source: Dark Empire endnotes ; Dark Empire 6 [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 134,8; approximate match 0.81, verify; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “He wiped out the Da Soocha moon base and the entire fleet of ships above it with this power.” [21]
  Source: Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 21; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Among the Emperor's powers was the ability to channel the collective life essences of billions to sustain himself and his Dark Side Adepts”; the passage says the entire population of Byss was kept under the spell until the planet was destroyed. [21][265][266]
  Source: The Essential Atlas [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 265; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- “Palpatine had a very wide-ranging Battle meditation, keeping his empire's military going with his powers, sometimes guiding a fleet or army.” The article specifically distinguishes Declann’s use at Endor from Palpatine’s own battle meditation there. [133][179][263]
  Source: Dark Empire Sourcebook [per Wookieepedia "Palpatine/Legends" rev 15710469, ref 133; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
